title: Recognition and functoriality of directed ring colimit cocones
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed poset and $(A_i,f_{ij})$ a diagram of commutative rings, with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{jk}f_{ij}=f_{ik}$ for $i\leq j\leq k$. Let $R$ be a commutative ring with ring homomorphisms $q_i:A_i\to R$ satisfying $q_jf_{ij}=q_i$. Assume every $r\in R$ is $q_i(a)$ for some $i,a$, and whenever $a,b\in A_i$ have $q_i(a)=q_i(b)$ there is $k\geq i$ with $f_{ik}(a)=f_{ik}(b)$. Then $(R,(q_i))$ is a colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in commutative rings, and its underlying cocones are colimits in abelian groups and sets. Explicitly, for every compatible cocone $t_i:A_i\to B$ of ring homomorphisms, of additive homomorphisms of the underlying abelian groups, or of functions of the underlying sets, respectively, there is exactly one map $t:R\to B$ of the respective kind satisfying $t(q_i(a))=t_i(a)$ for every $i,a$. For any other such ring diagram $(A'_i,f'_{ij})$ and cocone $(R',q'_i)$ satisfying the same two assumptions, and any compatible ring maps $u_i:A'_i\to A_i$ and $u:R'\to R$ with $u q'_i=q_i u_i$, the canonical colimit identifications commute with the induced colimit map in all three categories. The rings may be zero rings, and the maps need not be injective.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' to the underlying set cocone. The representation hypothesis supplies its surjectivity condition (with equality reversed); the same-stage eventual-equality hypothesis supplies its injectivity condition using homOfLE. The nonempty directed preorder is filtered. Mathlib constructs a filtered ring colimit and the forgetful functor to sets preserves filtered colimits and reflects isomorphisms, hence reflects this colimit. Therefore the supplied ring cocone is colimiting.

The composite forgetful functor from commutative rings through rings to additive commutative groups preserves filtered colimits, as does the forgetful functor to sets. Apply isColimitOfPreserves to obtain the other two colimit structures. Repeat the construction for the second diagram and cocone.

proof.text: For arbitrary chosen colimits d and d', prove each comparison square by IsColimit.hom_ext on the source colimit. On every coprojection, comp_coconePointUniqueUpToIso_hom and ι_map reduce the square to the assumed cocone compatibility. In additive groups and sets, apply the corresponding forgetful functor to this compatibility, using preservation of composition. This establishes naturality in all three categories.
